_comments: Former description, kept as the design note: The deal is live and progressing. The only status a new deal starts in.

fields.Name: Open
fields.Description: The deal is live and progressing. Every new deal starts here.

_comments: Former description, corrected: winning runs the pipeline's CloseWonPolicy (a contract when the policy asks for one, plus finance tasks) in one transaction. It creates no order: the deal's own order changes status on stage entry. It LOCKS the deal, because the deal is now the provenance of the contract and the order.

fields.Name: Won
fields.Description: The customer committed. Winning follows the pipeline's close-won policy and locks the deal.

_comments: Former description, kept as the design note: The customer chose otherwise. Requires a LossReason; locks the deal so the reason cannot be quietly revised later.

fields.Name: Lost
fields.Description: The customer chose otherwise. Requires a loss reason and locks the deal.

_comments: Former description, kept as the design note: We walked away, or the deal went dark. Counts as lost for win-rate and forecast purposes — the distinction from Lost is diagnostic, not behavioural, which is exactly why it is a separate ROW rather than a separate code path.

fields.Name: Abandoned
fields.Description: We walked away, or the deal went dark. Counts as lost in win rates and forecasts.

_comments: Former description, kept as the design note: Paused — neither progressing nor concluded, which is why it is neither IsOpen nor IsClosed. That combination is the reason those two flags are not each other's inverse: a rollup asking 'still live' and one asking 'not yet concluded' want different answers here.
